documents.text: The paper studies whether recent stock winners continue to outperform recent losers over intermediate horizons. It compares formation and holding windows, overlapping portfolios, and a short delay before investment. The selected development case uses six months of past returns, six-month overlapping holdings, and monthly equal-weight rebalancing without a skipped week. Its construction differs from a twelve-minus-two momentum signal.
documents.title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency

documents.source_version: June 2012 author manuscript; precursor to 2013 publication
documents.text: The manuscript examines gross profitability as a predictor of equity returns and its relationship to value. The selected annual strategy sorts firms by gross profits relative to assets, uses NYSE quintile breakpoints, excludes financial firms, and forms value-weighted portfolios at June end. The manuscript distinguishes annual accounting signals from faster quarterly variants and separates portfolio returns from factor-model alphas.
documents.title: The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium

documents.text: The paper separates earnings into accrual and cash-flow components and studies their persistence and subsequent stock returns. Its trading tests rank annual balance-sheet accruals scaled by average assets, buying low-accrual firms and selling high-accrual firms in equal-weighted deciles. Return measurement starts four months after fiscal year-end. The paper reports size-adjusted returns and Jensen alphas separately, with explicit treatment of delistings.
documents.title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings?
